title: Safehouse and Cover
premise: Tamsin Eriksen, a disgraced intelligence analyst haunted by an operation that killed her team, receives calls on a burner phone from her dead handler's voice — proof he faked his death and buried evidence of a covert program sold to the highest bidder. Hunted by an assassin working for the program's architect, her own former mentor, she must smuggle the archive past three governments who each want it silenced. In the end Tamsin chooses truth over survival, exposing the program at the cost of her last safe identity — and discovering the voice on the phone was never her handler at all.
about_author: Lior Crane is the pen name of a former policy researcher who writes espionage fiction from a small coastal town, drawing on years spent reading declassified archives. Safehouse and Cover is their third thriller and first to feature analyst Tamsin Eriksen.

chapters.title: The Number That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Tamsin, sleepless and semi-employed in Reykjavik, answers a burner phone delivered to her door. The voice is her dead handler Aldous Vey, reciting details only he knew about the failed Kola operation. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: dread curdling into desperate hope that her guilt might be misplaced.

chapters.title: Dead Men Dial Twice
chapters.summary: Vey directs her to a storage unit holding a fragment of the Meridian archive — records of a surveillance program auctioned across three governments. An assassin, Ilse Marchetti, arrives minutes behind her; Tamsin escapes with the drive but burns her apartment doing so. POV: Tamsin. Beat: fear sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Three Flags, One Grave
chapters.summary: In Oslo, Tamsin contacts a former colleague, Rune, to authenticate the drive while evading Norwegian intelligence, which wants Meridian buried. Flashbacks reveal the Kola incident was no accident — her team was sacrificed to protect the sale. POV: Tamsin with one Rune interlude. Beat: grief transmuting into rage.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Hand
chapters.summary: Tamsin learns the program's architect is Director Caspian Hale, her old mentor who recruited her. Hale sends a warm, threatening message offering reinstatement if she surrenders the drive. Marchetti closes in at a train station; Rune takes a bullet covering her escape. POV: Tamsin. Beat: betrayal layered over loss.

chapters.title: Safehouse Rules
chapters.summary: Holed up in a Baltic safehouse, Tamsin decrypts more of the archive and finds Vey listed as its original custodian — alive as of eight months ago. She realizes the calls may be genuine, or bait. Marchetti tracks her but hesitates, revealing she has her own grievance against Hale. POV: alternating Tamsin/Marchetti. Beat: wary alliance forming.

chapters.title: What the Archive Buys
chapters.summary: Tamsin and Marchetti trace the money: Meridian's buyers include officials in all three governments, meaning no agency can be trusted with the full file. Vey calls again with coordinates in Tallinn — and a warning that the archive is incomplete without a physical key. POV: Tamsin. Beat: isolation deepening; trust becoming a calculated risk.

chapters.title: Tallinn, Low Tide
chapters.summary: In Tallinn they retrieve the key from a sunken dead-drop, ambushed by Hale's second team. Marchetti saves Tamsin, confirming her defection, but is gravely wounded. Vey finally agrees to meet — at the lighthouse where Kola's orders were signed. POV: Tamsin. Beat: cost made flesh; resolve hardening.

chapters.title: The Voice at the Lighthouse
chapters.summary: The meeting: 'Vey' appears — but Tamsin's analysis catches the tells of a synthesized voice and a body double. The real Vey died at Kola; Hale built the lure to draw out every copy of the archive. Hale arrives to collect. POV: Tamsin. Beat: the floor drops out — betrayal complete, trap sprung.

chapters.title: Everything Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax. Captured aboard Hale's ship, Tamsin stalls him by dissecting his ego, while a wounded Marchetti breaches the hold. Tamsin triggers a staggered release: fragments to press in three countries simultaneously, unkillable now. Hale tries to destroy the ship and them with it. POV: Tamsin with Marchetti interlude. Beat: fury turned to cold execution.

chapters.title: No Cover Left
chapters.summary: Resolution. The Meridian files detonate across three governments; Hale vanishes into deniable ruin, hunted by his own buyers. Marchetti recovers under a new name; Tamsin testifies off-record, then walks away from every identity she had. Sleeping through the night for the first time since Kola, she mails one last burner phone to an unknown address. POV: Tamsin. Beat: costly peace, and a door left open.
